name: Glazed roof tile
summary: A roof tile of fine clay with a coloured lead glaze. The glaze makes the roof bright, hard and watertight, and its colour shows the rank of the building.
how: Press the tile from a fine, pale clay and fire it to a biscuit at about 1000 °C.
Dip or brush the biscuit with a lead glaze that has copper, iron or cobalt in it.
Lay half-round cover tiles over flat pan tiles in a bed of lime mortar.

origin.note: Chinese builders glaze roof tiles in the first centuries of the imperial age.

adoptions.via: Imperial kilns near Beijing make yellow, green and blue glazed tile for the roofs of the Forbidden City.
